ops.body:
Four independent astra reviews (correctness finder, security refuter, Darwin regression, ABWC contract) over a4c43d9..a92416a, synthesized by opus; full text under /Users/yasyf/.local/state/orca-workspace/recovery-20260930/cookiesync-linux/review/ (finder.md, security.md, darwin.md, contract.md, synthesis.md). Verdict REWORK; no security invariant refuted.

Must-fix accepted: M1 WindowAuto collapsed to headed in `rpc bridge_open` and cross-host forwarding; M2 arc as a second local browser in untagged tests (plus a hang on `<-consent.entered`); M3 fixtures without a `meta` table; M4 fixtures not isolating XDG_CONFIG_HOME; M5 remote browser targets validated against the local registry (fix: platform-independent `cookie.BrowserNames` for remote targets); M6 Secret Service lookup across all collections instead of Chrome's ReadAlias("default") collection; M7 `cookiesync uninstall` on a never-installed host fails inside daemonkit v0.32.1 `Client.Stop` → `inventoryClear` resolving a never-placed program; M8 chrome_crashpad leaves the daemonkit session.

Corrections from root (bus #162, #169, #176): the synthesis's proposed M7 upstream fix "return nil on fs.ErrNotExist in inventoryClear" is REJECTED by the reviewed daemonkit safety contract (recovery-20260930/daemonkit-never-installed-stop-review.md): the SDK patch instead delegates missing-path handling to proc.ExecutableIdentities and proves the observed pin departed via proc.Observe before clearing; it is being implemented by root's own Fable lane (yasyf/daemonkit-stop-inventory, base 9f699b43). cookiesync's `rpc.Stop` with `daemonkit.Program{}` is the documented weaker label-only contract, kept only until that patch releases; then cookiesync restores the real declared Program and bumps the pin before final merge. For M8 a test-side exemption of `chrome_crashpad` is NOT accepted: the fix is a narrowly tracked owned-process lifetime (handlers identified by the session's own crash database path, held by pidfd, reaped on Close) or a supported launcher switch, with the strict no-survivor check kept.

Should-fix accepted: S2 target parsing via BrowserNames, S3 scheme_store_test meta case, S4-S6 linux-smoke.sh assertion rigor. Rejected: the Darwin `--headed` help-text change (behavior identical for every flag combination), U6.md wording, duplicates.

Decisions: chromium dropped from the Linux registry (root #116/#133); Chrome discovery on Linux stays PATH-based (accepted by root in #162 within the single-UID VM trust model); the strict reading of #133 applies (Linux never mints the `local` principal, in-process callers included).
